chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jameela, from Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who blinded an eye of a man, (whose vision) had gone, and it (the eye) was firm. He (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is the quarter of the wergild of an eye.

key_terms.فَقَأَ: to blind or pierce the eye
key_terms.قَائِمَةٌ: firm/standing (referring to the eye remaining intact but now blind)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for blinding one eye when the other is already blind?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific calculation of *diyah* (blood money) for ocular injury, establishing that damaging a previously healthy eye when one is already blind incurs a quarter of the total eye compensation. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding proportional liability in cases of partial disability, reflecting the precise legal methodology of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in distinguishing between the loss of function and the loss of the organ itself.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abu Jameela, from Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, regarding a man who blinded an eye of a man, (whose vision) had gone, and it (the eye) was firm’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is the quarter of the wergild of an eye’.
